initial_presentation: A 7-year-old girl was presented with an abnormality of the right shoulder. On physical examination, the right scapula appeared smaller and positioned higher than usual, but shoulder movement was not restricted.

A 35-year-old Moroccan man presented with intermittent left flank pain and visible blood in his urine for the past 10 years. He had a history of passing stones on two occasions and had occasionally taken ibuprofen for pain relief. Physical examination showed he was in very good general condition, afebrile, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. He experienced slight left flank pain without a palpable mass. His body mass index (BMI) was 27 kg/m2. No other abnormalities were found on complete physical examination.

A 7-year-old boy presented to the Outpatient Department of Ophthalmology in July 2018 with complaints of photophobia, tearing, and blurred vision in both eyes. This was his third episode. He reported no fatigue and had no systemic diseases. He also denied recent contact with individuals with influenza or a cold. His birth history, growth history, and family history were unremarkable. He had experienced ocular irritation in both eyes twice before. The first episode occurred 4 months prior, lasting for 1 month, with symptoms of ocular pain, tearing, and photophobia. Ocular examination at that time revealed pin-like nebula in both corneas. Symptoms did not significantly improve after 2 weeks of local antiviral treatment but resolved dramatically after discontinuation of the eye drops.
A 36-year-old male was admitted due to progressively worsening vision in the left eye. Ophthalmologic evaluation of the retina showed no significant findings.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman. She was born at full term following an uneventful pregnancy. Her parents are not related by blood. During her first year of life, her development was mostly typical, although she exhibited unstable crawling, muscular hypotonia, and nystagmus. She began speaking her first words at 1 year old and formed her first sentences by 2 years old. She started walking at 1.5 years old, but her gait and balance were noted to be abnormal. At 3 years old, her cognitive development was evaluated as normal, with the exception of mild slowness and clumsiness in fine motor skills.

A 37-year-old Caucasian female from São Paulo, Brazil, delivered a healthy male infant in February 2009 via vaginal delivery at 40 weeks gestation. The newborn weighed 3510g and had Apgar scores of 9 and 10, with no obstetric complications. Within the first 24 hours, the infant developed petechiae and severe thrombocytopenia (14,000/mm3), while hemoglobin and white blood cell counts remained normal and there was no sign of infection. The newborn was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for further evaluation.
The patient, a 20-year-old female, reported experiencing recurrent episodes of fainting during physical activity since she was 9 years old.

A 34-year-old female presented with skin lesions on both lower limbs, accompanied by intense itching for the past 15 years. The lesions showed no seasonal variation and were absent in the oral cavity. No similar lesions were reported among family members. The patient had no history of diabetes or hypertension. Physical examination revealed lichenoid papules on both shins extending to the knees, which were non-tender and had mild scaling. There was no involvement of nails or mucosal areas.

A 68-year-old female patient arrived at the emergency department experiencing chest discomfort and palpitations. She has a history of untreated schizophrenia and anxiety. Endocrinology was consulted regarding adrenal nodules and hirsutism. The patient provided limited historical information and has been living alone for many years. Reports from nursing staff and adult services indicated that her brother mentioned she was previously labeled with a specific term and was kept away from the community by her mother. The patient reported having menstrual periods between the ages of 14 and 16, with no periods since then. She denied any recent changes in hair growth, skin, weight, or voice, although she had a long beard that was shaved by the nursing staff upon presentation. She was not sexually active and denied any history of surgeries, smoking, alcohol, or drug use. Her family history is unknown. Upon admission, her vital signs were as follows: temperature 98.6°F, pulse 105 beats per minute, blood pressure 145/111 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Physical examination revealed that she was awake, alert, and oriented to self. She had a masculine appearance with scanty hair on the scalp, bald spots anteriorly, shaved facial hair, excessive hair on the extremities and back, poor dentition, and well-developed breasts. Genitourinary examination showed pubic hair extending to the umbilicus, excess labial folds, no clitoromegaly, a small vaginal opening, and no palpable testicular tissue.

A 17-year-old female presented to the Liver Unit with severe jaundice, pruritus accompanied by scratching-induced hematomas, and generalized weakness over the past 2 months. She also reported amenorrhea, diarrhea, and a weight loss of approximately 10 kg during this period.
